title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Whether Staff Members of Compulsory Isolation Drug Rehabilitation Centers Can Become the Subjects of the Crime of Maltreating Persons Under Supervision

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Procuratorate
February 15, 2015
Reply of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Whether Staff Members of Compulsory Isolation and Detoxification Centers May Become Subjects of the Crime of Maltreating Persons under Supervision
(Adopted by the 34th Meeting of the Twelfth Procuratorial Committee
of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on January 29, 2015)
Gao Jian Fa Shi Zi [2015] No.2
The People's Procuratorate of Hebei Province:
Your Request for Instructions No. Ji Jian Cheng Zi [2014] 46 on Whether Staff Members of Compulsory Isolation and Detoxification Centers May Become Subjects of the Crime of Maltreating Persons under Supervision under Article 248 of the Criminal Law has been received. Upon study, the reply is as follows:
In accordance with relevant legal provisions, a compulsory isolation and detoxification center is a supervisory institution that restricts the personal liberty of drug addicts meeting specific conditions and conducts compulsory isolation and detoxification. Its staff members who perform supervisory duties fall within the category of "supervisory personnel" as provided in Article 248 of the Criminal Law.
Where a supervisory staff member of a compulsory isolation and detoxification center beats or physically punishes or maltreats a drug addict under detoxification, or instructs a drug addict to beat, physically punish, or maltreat another drug addict, if the circumstances are serious, the provisions of Article 248 of the Criminal Law shall be applied, and criminal liability shall be investigated for the crime of maltreating persons under supervision; if the consequences cause injury, disability, or death of the drug addict, the provisions of Articles 234 and 232 of the Criminal Law shall be applied, and the person shall be subjected to severe punishment for the crime of intentional injury or intentional homicide.
This reply is hereby given.
Supreme People's Procuratorate
February 15, 2015
